messages:
ari: Quick question  I'm adding a short "Rate limits & Dedicated" subsection to the provisioning guide. It needs: 1) an example showing routing-level quotas + tenant-level QPS in the same YAML, 2) a tiny Python SDK snippet, and 3) one-line SLA language about quotas vs reserved-pool availability. Can docs/infra sanity-check?

+danny: Nice. Make it explicit that rate limits are enforced at the API gateway layer and are orthogonal to capacity provisioning. Also call out `burst_window_seconds` so folks don't confuse it with cooldown.

priya: Paste the minimal YAML you plan to include and I'll turn it into a short SDK example.

ari: Draft YAML for the provisioning examples section:
```yaml
reserved_capacity:
  tenant_id: "tenant-qos-7"
  nodes: 6
  isolation:
    decorator: tenant-qos
    preemption: false
  quotas:
    tenant_qps: 2000           # tenant-wide sustained QPS
    per_route_quota:
      /v1/generate: 1500      # route-level cap
      /v1/embed: 1000
    burst_window_seconds: 30  # burst allowance window
```

priya: Python SDK snippet (very short):
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient()
c.apply_reserved_policy('tenant-qos-7', {
  'nodes': 6,
  'isolation': {'decorator': 'tenant-qos', 'preemption': False},
  'quotas': {'tenant_qps': 2000, 'per_route_quota': {'/v1/generate': 1500, '/v1/embed': 1000}, 'burst_window_seconds': 30}
})
```

danny: SLA wording suggestion: "Rate limits (tenant_qps, per_route_quota) are operational controls applied at ingress to protect capacity and fairness; they do not modify reserved-pool uptime SLAs. If you need higher sustained throughput than your reserved pool supports, request additional dedicated capacity through Support."

priya: Migration note (short): "Legacy fields: `rate_limit_rps` -> `tenant_qps`; `route_shaper` -> `per_route_quota`; `burst_ms` -> `burst_window_seconds` (divide by 1000)."

ari: Add a short callout about isolation interaction: "Using `decorator: tenant-qos` increases scheduling priority for this tenant and reduces noisy-neighbor risk, but rate limits are still enforced at the gateway and can throttle even if nodes are available."

docs-bot: preview created for PR #2799  https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-2799 (lint OK)

infra-bot: infra QA: will run a gateway+placement sim tomorrow to validate that burst_window_seconds behaves as documented (ops will paste results).

priya: Tiny CLI example for copy-paste: `redwoodctl reserved apply --tenant tenant-qos-7 --nodes 6 --isolation tenant-qos --no-preempt --tenant-qps 2000 --route /v1/generate=1500 --route /v1/embed=1000 --burst 30`

danny: One more doc nit: add a short sentence that burst allowances are consumed across routes (not per-route) unless `per_route_quota` is configured, so folks don't assume unlimited cross-route bursts.

ari: Great point  I'll include that sentence and merge after the preview looks good. Thanks all! :thumbsup:

ari: Merged and added the example to the Dedicated quickstart under "Rate limiting and QoS". Closing thread.
